subject: home-science
general_outcomes: Apply knowledge on nutritive value of food to prevent and manage nutritional deficiency diseases and disorders for healthy living.
Utilise knowledge, skills and attitudes in meal planning, preparation, cooking, presentation and preservation of food for a healthy life.
Exploit individual talents in food preparation, cooking and service for leisure, self-fulfillment and entrepreneurship.
Develop skills for proper care of the home, care and maintenance of clothes and household articles in day-to-day life.
Apply principles of consumer education for family financial management
Choose fabrics for various uses based on their different characteristics.
Apply various techniques in drafting and grading basic pattern blocks for constructing garments.
Construct garments using various clothing construction techniques.
Appreciate Home science as a subject and the role it plays in improving the life of an individual, family and the nation.

substrands.name: Overview of Foods and Nutrition
learning_outcomes: explain the importance of foods and nutrition as an area of study in Home Science
identify careers related to foods and nutrition
appreciate the role of foods and nutrition in our day-to-day life.
learning_experiences: discuss the importance of foods and nutrition as an area of study in Home Science
use digital and print resources to search for information on various career opportunities related to foods and nutrition
Participate in career talks in Clubs and Societies with peers, design a career wheel and mount it on the classroom wall.
inquiry_questions: How can the knowledge of foods and nutrition inform career opportunities?
core_competencies: Learners display team work and are able to speak clearly and effectively while discussing the significance of foods and nutrition learnt in Home science.
Creativity and imagination: The Learner undertake tasks that show ability to use imagination to generate new ideas as they design a career wheel.
values: Respect: learner recognizes and respects the input of every member of the team as they discuss on the significance of foods and nutrition.
pertinent_issues: Career guidance: Learners participate in career talks with peers to make informed decisions on their career pathway.

substrands.name: Kitchen Layouts and Equipment

describe tools and equipment used in the kitchen
care for tools and equipment used in the kitchen
appreciate the importance of different layouts, tools and equipment in the kitchen.

brainstorm on factors to consider when choosing kitchen layouts, tools and equipment
observe pictures or realia to identify and classify kitchen tools and equipment

values: Values:
Responsibility: The learner cares for own equipment and those of others as they carry out cleaning and storage of the kitchen equipment.

Unity: Learners promote teamwork as they carry out group tasks during research on materials used to make kitchen tools and equipment. Pertinent and Contemporary Issues (PCIs): Health education: Learners promote health when caring for kitchen tools and equipment through cleaning.

substrands.name: Food Hygiene and safety
learning_outcomes: explain the importance of hygiene and safety when handling food
differentiate between food spoilage and poisoning when handling food
apply hygiene practices when handling food
adopt high hygiene standards when handling food.
learning_experiences: discuss the importance of food hygiene and safety when handling food

use digital and print resources to search for the difference between food spoilage and poisoning (meaning, causes, signs, and prevention) then share findings with peers Note: (causes; chemicals, micro-organisms, poor storage, poor handling of food, pests and insects; signs; change in colour, change in texture, unpleasant smell, undesirable taste)
observe spoilt food and identify signs of spoilage
practise hygiene when handling food.
inquiry_questions: 1. Why is food spoilage and poisoning a concern when handling food?
2. How can we adopt safe habits and proper hygiene when handling food?

values: Values: Integrity: the learner applies laid down food hygiene procedures when handling food to promote safety. Pertinent and Contemporary Issues (PCIs): Health education: Learners promote health as they observe food hygiene practices and safety.

substrands.name: Methods of Cooking
learning_outcomes: classify methods of cooking food
cook food using different methods
adopt use of different methods of cooking food.
learning_experiences: discuss reasons for cooking food and present in class

use digital and print resources to search on the categories of methods of cooking, general rules, advantages and disadvantages. (moist heat; boiling, stewing, steaming, poaching, frying, dry heat; roasting, grilling, baking)
prepare (cleaning, blending, kneading, mixing, cutting; chopping, slicing, peeling grating and dicing) and cook food using the different methods
observe safety while preparing and cooking food using the different methods.
inquiry_questions: Why is knowledge on methods of cooking important?
core_competencies: Self-efficacy: Learners show a concerted attention to detail as they apply the knowledge of cooking methods to prepare food items.
Digital literacy: Learners use digital devices to effectively accomplish own tasks when they research on categories of cooking.
values: Values:
Unity: Learners promote team work as they collaborate in accomplishing assigned tasks.
Integrity: Learners use resources well as they cook food using the different cooking. Pertinent and Contemporary Issues (PCIs):
Health education: Learners are sensitised on health and nutrition issues as they discuss in groups reasons for cooking food and present in class.
Safety: learners observe safety measures as they prepare and cook food.

substrands.name: Nutritive Value of Foods
learning_outcomes: Classify food nutrients according to the food groups
analyse the role of food nutrients in the body
plan meals from different food groups for proper nutrition
appreciate different foods from various food groups.
learning_experiences: discuss and make presentations on classification of food nutrients (carbohydrates, proteins, vitamins, fats, mineral salts), their sources and functions and group them (energy giving, protective, body building, Including dietary fibre and water)

search for information from digital or print media, discuss with a resource person on fortification and enrichment of foods in improvement of nutritional value (meaning, reasons for, relevant examples), then write reports

• formulate meal plans using locally available foods to address nutritional deficiencies and disorders.

2. why does the food you choose to eat affect your health?

Learning to learn: as learners carry out research on classes, functions and sources of food nutrients, and as they engage with the resource person.

Social justice: learners promote social justice as they share learning resources during research, and during cooking of meals.
Unity: Learners promote teamwork and unity as they carry out group tasks on research and cooking of food.
pertinent_issues: Health education: the learner gains knowledge in health and recognise the importance of food nutrients in prevention of nutritional deficiency diseases.
